info.title: rust-dns API
info.description:
Management API of the rust-dns authoritative DNS server.

**Authentication.** Either
* a cookie session: `POST /auth/login` (then `/auth/mfa` if MFA is enabled) sets the `rdns_session` cookie, which the browser sends automatically; or
* an API token: `Authorization: Bearer rdns_...` (create one under *Tokens*; use the **Authorize** button).

**CSRF guard.** Cookie-authenticated writes (POST/PUT/DELETE) must send the header `X-Requested-With: rust-dns`, otherwise they fail with 403 `code: csrf`. The Swagger UI in the web console adds this header automatically. Bearer-token requests do not need it.

**Live server.** "Try it out" sends real requests to this server with the caller's permissions: changes are committed, logged and served over DNS immediately.

Errors are JSON `{"error": "...", "code": null|"..."}`. Zones the caller cannot see return 404.

This document is generated from the server's code, so it always matches the running version.

post.description: Checks username and password and starts a cookie session. Depending on the account the session is active at once or still needs a TOTP code (`/auth/mfa`) or forced MFA enrollment (`/auth/enroll`).

200.description: Credentials accepted. Sets the session cookie; check `status` for the next step.

Set-Cookie.description: `rdns_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` over plain HTTP; `__Host-rdns_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure` over HTTPS (a trusted proxy sent `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`) or with `secure_cookies = true`.

post.summary: Sign in (step 2): TOTP or recovery code
post.description: For a session in `mfa_required` state (cookie from /auth/login). Accepts a 6-digit TOTP code or a one-time recovery code.

For a session in `enroll_required` state: confirm the secret from the login response with a TOTP code. On a read-only standby only the local root account can enroll here (other accounts are replicated from the primary: enroll there).

200.description: Enrolled; session active. Recovery codes are shown once.

get.summary: State of the current cookie session
get.description: Lets a client resume the right sign-in step. Never fails for a missing or expired cookie: that is `anonymous`.

200.description: Session state (`anonymous` without a valid cookie).

post.description: Deletes the cookie session if there is one. Always succeeds.

200.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared.

get.summary: Current user, client IP and auth method

put.description: Needs an interactive (cookie) session. Not available to root, whose password is set in the configuration file. Every other session of the user is signed out; API tokens keep working (revoke them separately).

post.description: Needs an interactive (cookie) session. Replacing an already enrolled authenticator also needs the current TOTP code or the password.

requestBody.description: Only when MFA is already enrolled (replacing the authenticator): the current TOTP `code` or the account `password`. Otherwise send no body or `{}`.

200.description: Secret, otpauth URI and QR SVG; confirm with /me/mfa/confirm.

post.description: Confirms the secret from /me/mfa/start with a TOTP code.
Not allowed when MFA is required for the account. Needs a current TOTP code.
Needs a current TOTP code; the previous recovery codes stop working.

200.description: New recovery codes (old ones stop working).

post.description: Needs an interactive (cookie) session; keeps the current one.
Needs `create_zones`. The owner defaults to the caller.

get.summary: Zone with the first page of records and its members

put.description: Needs the owner role; changing `owner` needs `transfer_ownership` (administrators). Omitted fields are unchanged.

delete.summary: Delete a zone and all its records

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text matched against name, type and value.

post.description: Needs the editor role. To register a name that disappears unless renewed, send `expires_in` (seconds) or `expires_at`; posting the identical record again with a new expiry renews it (200).

expiring.summary: Self-registration: A record that expires in 24 hours unless renewed

200.description: Renewed: an identical record (same name, type and value) already existed and the request carried an expiry, or the existing one had expired. Its expiry was replaced.

put.description: Needs the editor role. Send only the fields you change: omitted fields, including `ttl`, keep their current values. Send `"ttl": null` to switch to the zone default TTL.
Needs the owner role on the zone.

delete.description: Needs the owner role on the zone.

get.summary: Effective rights of a user or of their API tokens
get.description: Administrators may read anyone's; users their own.

parameters.name: via
parameters.description: `token` shows what the user's API tokens may do.

200.description: Rights generated from the same permission table the API enforces.

get.description: Signing state, the key (public part), the DS records for the registrar and the signature window. Needs the viewer role.

put.summary: Turn DNSSEC signing on or off
put.description: Needs the owner role. **On**: the zone is signed from now on (a key is generated the first time). Nothing changes for resolvers until the DS record is published at the registrar. **Off**: refused with 409 `ds_published` while the parent publishes a DS for the zone (or when that cannot be checked): remove the DS at the registrar first and wait for its TTL. `force: true` skips that check.

get.summary: DS records to publish at the registrar
get.description: SHA-256 (digest type 2, publish this one) and SHA-384 (4) DS records of the zone's key. Empty before signing was ever turned on. Needs the viewer role.

get.summary: Check this server's signed answers (before adding the DS)
get.description: Queries this server's own answers with the DO bit (DNSKEY, SOA, NS, a sample of names, a name that does not exist, a missing type) and validates every signature and denial-of-existence proof with the zone's key. Only this server is checked: other name servers of the zone are not. Needs the viewer role; 409 while signing is off.

get.summary: Is the DS published at the parent?
get.description: Looks up the zone's DS record through the first forwarding upstream (a recursive resolver) and compares it with the zone's key: `present` (matches), `absent`, `mismatch` (a DS for another key: validating resolvers fail the zone) or `unknown` (no upstream configured, or the lookup failed). Needs the viewer role.

get.summary: Export all visible zones as JSON

post.description: Callers with `create_zones` may create zones; others can only import into zones where they are owner.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
`merge` adds missing zones and records; `replace` replaces the records
of each zone in the document.

post.summary: Import a hosts file into a zone
post.description: Reads `/etc/hosts`-format text and adds its A / AAAA records to the zone in one transaction (same `merge` / `replace` modes as the JSON import). Names outside the zone are listed and skipped. `preview: true` changes nothing. Needs the zone's import permission (owner).

200.description: Parsed records, skipped names and (unless a preview) the import summary.

get.description: One row per committed fact (zone, record, serial, member); rows from one transaction share `txn` and `command`. Rolled-back operations never appear. Non-admins see only their zones; membership rows and other users' `actor_ip` (empty string) only on zones they own.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Return entries after this offset/id (oldest first). Omit for the most
recent entries.

get.description: Users, MFA, recovery codes, sessions, API tokens, root sync. Each entry was written in the same transaction as the change. Needs `view_audit`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Return entries after this offset/id (oldest first). Omit for the most
recent entries.

get.summary: WebSocket stream (not callable from Swagger UI)
get.description:
WebSocket upgrade; Swagger UI cannot open it, use a WebSocket client. Streams change events (resumable with `after`) and, with `queries=true`, live DNS queries for zones the caller owns.

Browsers authenticate with the session cookie; the page's `Origin` must match the host. Other clients send an API token as a subprotocol: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: rust-dns, rust-dns.bearer.<token>` (the server selects `rust-dns`), e.g. `websocat --protocol 'rust-dns, rust-dns.bearer.rdns_...' ws://host/api/ws?after=0`. `?token=` still works but is deprecated: URLs end up in proxy logs.

The stream re-checks the credentials and zone rights every 10 seconds and on membership changes; when the session or token is revoked or the account is disabled it closes with code 1008.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Replay change events after this offset first (WAL-style cursor).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Deprecated: API token in the URL (ends up in logs). Use the `rust-dns.bearer.<token>` subprotocol.

101.description: Switching protocols. Text frames are JSON: `{"type":"hello",...}`, `{"type":"change","event":ChangeEvent}`, `{"type":"query","event":QueryEvent}`, `{"type":"resync","head":N}` (see the ChangeEvent and QueryEvent schemas).

put.description: All fields optional. Changing the password or disabling the account signs the user out everywhere.

post.summary: Reset a user's MFA and sign them out (admin)

get.description: Active tokens with their tags, last use time and last client IP. Filter with `tag` (exact, case-sensitive match).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only tokens carrying exactly this tag (case-sensitive, surrounding spaces ignored).

200.description: Tokens (own, or everyone's with `all=true` for admins).

post.description: The token acts with exactly the caller's rights. Tokens do not expire; revoke them when no longer needed. Optional `tags` label the token (change them later with `PUT /tokens/{id}`).

201.description: Created. The plaintext token is returned only once.

put.description: Replaces the tag list. Own tokens; administrators (`manage_users`) may update anyone's. Revoked tokens cannot be changed (404). A change is recorded in the audit log as `token.update` with the tags before and after.

delete.description: Own tokens; administrators may revoke anyone's.

get.description: Cheap database ping (no integrity scan). No authentication.
Generated from the server's route and type definitions, so it always matches the running server.

get.summary: Server status, counters and runtime settings

post.description: Re-reads the configuration file and applies runtime settings. Needs `server_admin`.

get.description: Runs `PRAGMA quick_check` over the whole database; may be slow on large databases. Needs `server_admin`.

Upstream resolvers, allowed client networks and timeout currently in effect, whether they come from the config file or were saved from the console, and the config file's own values. Needs `server_admin`.

put.description: Saves forwarding settings that override `[forwarding]` in the config file and applies them at once (no restart). The change and its audit entry are one transaction. `open_resolver: true` deliberately allows any client network (e.g. `0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`) and turns on the open-resolver safeguards; see the README before using it. Needs `server_admin`.

delete.summary: Use the config file's forwarding settings again (admin)
delete.description: Removes the console override; `[forwarding]` from the config file applies at once. No-op when there is no override. Needs `server_admin`.

post.description: Sends a recursive `. NS` query to each upstream over UDP and reports whether and how fast it answered. Nothing is saved. Needs `server_admin`.

200.description: One result per upstream, in order.

post.description: Drops every cached forwarded answer; the next queries go to the upstreams. Audited as `settings.forwarding.cache_flush`. Needs `server_admin`.

get.description: Settings for forwarded queries (domain-needed, bogus-priv, rebinding protection, serve stale, upstream strategy, filtered types, EDNS Client Subnet), whether they were saved from the console, and what this server observed: upstream health, names refused by rebinding protection, counters. Needs `server_admin`.

put.description: Saves the resolver settings and applies them at once (no restart); replicated to standbys. Omitted fields take their defaults. The change and its audit entry (`settings.resolver.update`) are one transaction. Needs `server_admin`.

delete.summary: Use the default resolver settings again (admin)
delete.description: Removes the saved resolver settings; the defaults apply at once (domain-needed and bogus-priv on, everything else off, upstreams in order). Audited as `settings.resolver.reset`. No-op when nothing is saved. Needs `server_admin`.

get.description: The blocklist configuration (replicated) and, per list, this server's last download, entries in use, errors and blocked queries. Blocklists apply to forwarded queries only. Needs `server_admin`.

put.description: Saves the list URLs, allowlist, block action and refresh interval; replicated to standbys, each server downloads the lists itself (new lists at once). Audited as `settings.blocklists.update`. Needs `server_admin`.

post.description: Starts a download of every enabled list on this server (not replicated); the result shows in `GET /blocklists` when it finishes. Needs `server_admin`.

Checks a name against the allowlist and every list in use on this server. Own and override zones are answered before blocklists, so a name they hold is never blocked whatever this says. Needs `server_admin`.

get.description: Names, algorithms and zone scopes. Secrets are never listed. Needs `server_admin`.

post.description: Generates a random secret, or imports `secret` (base64) when the secondary provider generated the key. The secret is returned only in this response (later: `POST /tsig/keys/{name}/reveal`, audited). Recorded in the audit log as `tsig.create` without the secret. Takes effect at once. Needs `server_admin`.

generate.summary: Generate a secret, key limited to one zone

import.summary: Import a secret from the secondary provider, all zones

201.description: Created. The secret is shown only here.

put.summary: Change the zones a TSIG key may transfer (admin)
put.description: Replaces the zone scope; an empty list allows every zone. The secret and algorithm cannot be changed (create a new key and delete the old one). Recorded as `tsig.update`. Needs `server_admin`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Key name, with or without the trailing dot (`hn-secondary.`).

delete.description: Secondaries using it can no longer transfer; NOTIFY configured with it is no longer sent. Recorded as `tsig.delete`. Needs `server_admin`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Key name, with or without the trailing dot (`hn-secondary.`).

post.summary: Show a TSIG key's secret (admin, audited)
post.description: Returns the base64 secret, e.g. to configure another secondary. Every call is recorded in the audit log as `tsig.reveal` (without the secret). Needs `server_admin`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Key name, with or without the trailing dot (`hn-secondary.`).

get.description: Allowed networks, whether TSIG is required, and NOTIFY targets with their keys, from `[transfer]` in the config file (edit the file and reload to change them). Needs `server_admin`.

get.summary: Role and history of this server (public)
get.description: No authentication. A primary with `[peer]` asks its standby this at startup and periodically: if the peer is writable and its `parent_history_id` is the asking server's history id, the peer was promoted and the asking server stays read-only (fenced). Contains no secrets and no data.

Role (primary, promoted, standby, fenced), history, and on a standby the connection to the primary: applied offset, lag, last error, last snapshot and reconcile. On a primary: its replicas (standbys by instance id, with state and lag). A standby also calls this on its primary to validate its token. Needs `replicate`.

parameters.name: X-Rust-DNS-Instance
parameters.description: Sent by standbys (their `[follow].instance_id`): the call counts as a sign of life.

get.summary: Consistent copy of all replicated data (admin, contains secrets)
get.description: Zones, records (with expiry state), zone members, users (password hashes, MFA secrets and last TOTP step, recovery code hashes), API token hashes and tags, console settings, TSIG keys, the history and the changelog offset it corresponds to, all read in one transaction. A standby loads it to start and whenever it cannot continue from the changelog (afterwards every change, account changes included, arrives through `/replication/changes`). Needs `replicate`; refused (409) on a server that is not a writable primary.

parameters.name: X-Rust-DNS-Session
parameters.description: Random per standby process (detects two processes with one instance id).

get.description: Committed changelog entries after `after`, DNS and account changes in one sequence (account changes carry password hashes, TOTP and TSIG secrets and appear nowhere else), whole transactions only, with the history id and the latest offset. The `after` of each request is recorded as the standby's applied offset (a standby commits a batch before asking for the next), unless `probe=true`. With `wait`, an answer without changes is held until a change commits or the wait ends. `gap: true`: entries after `after` were pruned or scrubbed; load a snapshot. Needs `replicate`; refused (409) on a server that is not a writable primary.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return changes after this offset (0: from the start).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
At most this many changes (extended to the end of the last
transaction), 1-5000.

parameters.name: probe
parameters.description: Health probe of the standby: do not record `after` as its applied offset.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
Seconds to wait for a change (or an account-data change) when there
is none yet, 0-60.

parameters.name: X-Rust-DNS-Session
parameters.description: Random per standby process (detects two processes with one instance id).

get.summary: Checksums of every replicated table and zone (admin)
get.description: SHA-256 of every replicated table (per-server columns such as token last use left out, and the rows of the account named `exclude_user`: the standby's own root, which is local there) and serial and SHA-256 of every zone, at one changelog offset. A standby compares them periodically (`[follow].reconcile_interval_secs`) and re-bootstraps on a mismatch. Needs `replicate`; refused (409) on a server that is not a writable primary.

parameters.name: exclude_user
parameters.description: Leave this account out (the standby's own config root).

parameters.name: X-Rust-DNS-Session
parameters.description: Random per standby process (detects two processes with one instance id).

post.description: Stops following, removes `[follow]` from the config file, starts a new history (parent: the old one, forked at the current offset), and accepts writes from now on. Refused (409) on a server that is not a standby, and while the primary is reachable unless `force` is true. Needs `replicate`. Audited as `replication.promote`.

get.description: Every standby known by its `[follow].instance_id`: state (`up_to_date`, `catching_up`, `falling_behind`, `offline`, `bootstrapping`; thresholds in `[replication]`), a `conflict` flag when two processes use one id, applied offset (the `after` of its last changes request), lag in changes and in seconds since it was last caught up, last seen, address, version. Kept in a local table across restarts; entries not seen for `[replication].forget_after_days` are dropped. Needs `replicate`.

delete.description: Removes the instance from the replica list (e.g. a decommissioned standby). A standby that is still running reappears at its next request. Local bookkeeping: audited as `replication.replica_forget`, not in the changelog and not replicated. Needs `replicate`.

post.summary: A standby reports that it stopped (admin)
post.description: Sent by a standby whose replication halted (its data diverged from this primary: a bug), once when it halts and once at each start while halted, so the replica list shows it as `halted` with the reason. The `X-Rust-DNS-Instance` header must name the same instance. Local bookkeeping (not audited, not in the changelog). Needs `replicate`.

example.detail: reconcile at offset 1834 found data that differs from the primary: table users: differs (3 rows here, 3 on the primary)

get.description: Mounted at the server root (`/metrics`), not under `/api`. Requires authentication (a bearer API token for scrapers).

text/plain.example:
# HELP rustdns_queries_total DNS queries received
# TYPE rustdns_queries_total counter
rustdns_queries_total 0

AuditRecord.description: A committed audit row, as stored and returned by the API.

txn.description: Shared by every row written in the same transaction.

BlockAction.description: What a blocked name is answered with.

BlockMatch.description: Why a name is blocked: the list and the entry that matched.

entry.description: The entry that matched (the name or a parent of it).

BlockTest.description: The outcome of a name test (`POST /blocklists/test`).

name.description: The name tested (lower-case, no trailing dot).

blocked.description: Blocked (forwarded queries for it are answered by the block action).

allowed_by.description: The allowlist entry that exempts it, if any.

BlockTestInput.description: A name to test against the blocklists.

BlocklistSettings.description: The blocklist configuration (replicated; downloads are per server).

allow.description:
Domains never blocked (suffix match: `example.com` also allows
`www.example.com`).

refresh_hours.description: Hours between downloads of each list (1 to 168).

url.description:
`https://` (or `http://`) URL of a hosts file, a plain list of
domains or an Adblock-style list (`||domain^`); the format is
detected per line.

BlocklistView.description: Blocklist configuration and this server's download state.

lists.description:
Per list: entries in use, last download, errors, blocked queries
(this server).

entries.description:
Domains in use over all enabled lists (before de-duplication across
lists).

memory_bytes.description: Memory held by the lists in use, bytes.

blocked.description: Forwarded queries blocked since start (this server).

ChangeEvent.description: One changelog entry; also the event broadcast after every mutation.

payload.description:
The exact committed fact, tagged by `kind`: zone_created, zone_updated,
zone_deleted, record_created, record_updated, record_deleted,
serial_bumped, member_set, member_removed.

txn.description: Shared by every row committed in the same transaction.

command.description: Operation that produced the change (create_record, import, ...).

ChangelogPage.description: Change log entries plus retention bounds.

resync_required.description: `after` fell behind retention; refetch full state.

ChangesResponse.description:
One long-poll answer: committed changes after the cursor (whole
transactions only), DNS and account changes in one sequence.

gap.description:
The cursor fell behind retention (changelog pruned, or account
changes scrubbed after `[changelog].account_retention_days`): fetch a
snapshot.

Checksums.description: Checksums of every replicated table, and per zone, at one offset.

code.description: 6-digit TOTP code (or, for /auth/mfa, a recovery code).

forwarded.description: Answers forwarded to an upstream resolver.

cache_hits.description: Forwarded answers served from the cache.

bad_cookie.description: Requests with an invalid or malformed DNS cookie.

tsig_errors.description: Signed requests rejected (unknown key, bad signature, clock skew, truncated MAC).

open_resolver_truncated.description:
Open resolver mode: forwarded UDP answers sent truncated because they
exceeded `[forwarding].open_resolver_max_udp_payload`.

open_resolver_any.description:
Open resolver mode: ANY queries for foreign names answered with the
minimal RFC 8482 HINFO instead of being forwarded.

open_resolver_rate_limited.description:
Open resolver mode: forwarded queries over
`[forwarding].open_resolver_rate_per_second` for their client.

forward_overflow.description:
Queries not forwarded (UDP dropped, TCP SERVFAIL) because
`[forwarding].max_inflight` forwarded queries were already waiting
for an upstream.

stale_answers.description:
Stale cache entries served because every upstream failed (serve
stale, RFC 8767).

DnssecCheck.description: This server's own signed answers, validated with the zone's key.

checks.detail: NOERROR, 1 answer and 0 authority RRsets verified

example.note: These are this server's answers only; validating resolvers start checking once the DS is published at the parent.

enabled.description:
true: sign the zone (a key is generated the first time); false: stop
signing (the key is kept, turning signing on again reuses it).

force.description:
Turning off: skip the check that the parent publishes no DS. Only
when the DS is already gone from the registrar and its TTL passed but
the check cannot confirm it. With a DS still published, the zone
fails to resolve for every validating resolver.

new_key.description:
Turning on while off: replace the kept key with a new one (a new DS
must then be published at the registrar).

DnssecKeyView.description: The zone's signing key (public part only).

flags.description: 257 = zone key and secure entry point (one combined signing key).

dnskey.description: The DNSKEY record in zone-file form.

enabled.description: Signing is on for this zone.

oneOf.description: Present once a key exists (signing was turned on at least once).

ds.description: DS records for the registrar (empty without a key).

oneOf.description: The signatures currently served (null when not signing).

standby.description:
This server is a read-only standby: it signs in memory with the
replicated key and never re-signs by itself.

DsList.description: The DS records of the zone's key.

key_tag.description: Null when the zone has no key yet.

DsRecordView.description: A DS record for the parent zone (the registrar).

recommended.description: The one to publish unless the registrar asks for another digest.

qr_svg.description: SVG QR code of `otpauth_uri` (null if it could not be rendered).

Error.description: Every non-2xx JSON error has this shape.

oneOf.description:
Machine-readable reason when one applies: `login_required`,
`mfa_required`, `enroll_required` (401) or `csrf` (403, cookie write
without `X-Requested-With: rust-dns`). `invalid_request`: the request
could not be parsed (malformed JSON, wrong field type or value,
unparsable path or query parameter, missing JSON content type).
`read_only_standby` (409): this server is a read-only standby; write
to the primary named in the message. `ds_published` (409): DNSSEC
signing cannot be turned off while the parent publishes a DS.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable reason carried by some errors.

ExportRecord.description:
One record of an export document; `ttl: null` (or omitted) means the
zone default.

expires_at.description: Exported expiry. Records already expired at import time are skipped.

ExportZone.description:
One zone of an export document. On import, omitted SOA fields fall back
to the server defaults (new zones) or are left unchanged.

override.description:
An override zone's settings (I1). On import they apply to a zone
the import creates; an existing zone keeps its type.

FilterStatus.description: One filter of the chain in effect, with its counters since start.

handled.description: Queries this filter saw (answered + dropped + passed).

passed.description: Queries passed to the next filter.

panicked.description: Queries that made this filter panic (answered SERVFAIL).

instance_id.description: This standby's `[follow].instance_id` (its name on the primary).

state.description: connecting | bootstrapping | following | error | refused | halted | stopped

connected.description: The last request to the primary succeeded.

primary_head.description: The primary's latest offset at the last contact.

lag_changes.description: Changes behind the primary (as of the last contact).

disconnected_since.description: Unreachable or refused since (null while connected).

ForwardCacheInfo.description: Forwarding cache size and counters since start.

hit_rate.description: hits / (hits + misses); 0 when there were no lookups.

ForwardingFileValues.description: Forwarding values from the config file (shown next to an override).

ForwardingInput.description:
New forwarding settings. Upstreams are IP addresses with an optional port
(53 when omitted): `1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8:53`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`,
`[2001:4860:4860::8888]:53`. Host names are not accepted.

upstreams.description: At most 8, tried in order. An empty list turns forwarding off.

allowed_clients.description:
CIDR networks or single addresses. Unless `open_resolver` is true,
anything that would make this an open resolver is refused: an entry
shorter than /8 (IPv4) or /16 (global IPv6), or entries covering over
1/16 of IPv4 together. An empty list means no client may use
forwarding, also in open resolver mode (list `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`).

cache_max_ttl.description:
Cap on how long positive answers are cached, 1 to 604800 seconds.
Omitted: the config file's `cache_max_ttl`.

cache_negative_max_ttl.description:
Cap on how long negative answers are cached, 1 to 604800 seconds and
not above the positive cap. Omitted: the config file's value.

open_resolver.description:
Deliberately run an open resolver: lifts the `allowed_clients` guard
and turns on the open-resolver safeguards. Omitted: the config file's
`open_resolver` (the saved override always records the value used).

Open resolver mode is in effect (`[forwarding].open_resolver` or the
console setting, with upstreams set): any client in `allowed_clients`,
possibly everyone, may resolve through this server.

upstreams.description: Upstream resolvers in effect, `ip:port`, tried in order. Empty: foreign names are refused.

allowed_clients.description: Client networks allowed to use forwarding.

updated_by.description: Who saved the override (`null` when the config file applies).

updated_at.description: When the override was saved (`null` when the config file applies).

cache_max_ttl.description: Longest a positive answer is cached, seconds (in effect).

cache_negative_max_ttl.description: Longest a negative answer is cached, seconds (in effect).

open_resolver.description:
Open resolver mode in effect: `allowed_clients` may cover any
network (e.g. `0.0.0.0/0`) and, whenever queries are forwarded, the
safeguards apply (UDP answers
over `open_resolver_max_udp_payload` truncated, ANY not forwarded,
per-client forwarding rate limit).

open_resolver_max_udp_payload.description:
Largest forwarded UDP answer in open resolver mode, bytes
(`[forwarding].open_resolver_max_udp_payload`, config file only).

open_resolver_rate_per_second.description:
Forwarded queries per second per client in open resolver mode; 0 = no
extra limit (`[forwarding].open_resolver_rate_per_second`, config file only).

max_inflight.description:
Most forwarded queries waiting for an upstream at one time; over it
UDP queries are dropped and TCP queries get SERVFAIL
(`[forwarding].max_inflight`, config file only).

config.description: The config file's values, for comparison and reset.

GlobalPerm.description: Something a caller may do outside any one zone.

GlobalRight.description: One account-level permission and whether the user holds it.

HaltInfo.description:
A standby stopped following because its data diverged from the primary
(a bug: a standby never changes replicated data by itself). Kept until
the operator rebuilds it with `rust-dns --prepare-standby --yes`.

detail.description: What exactly differed (tables, zones, checksums, offsets).

offset.description: This standby's changelog offset when it halted.

report_file.description: The divergence report written next to the database.

History.description:
Where a database's data comes from. A primary gets a random
`history_id` on first start; a standby adopts its primary's lineage at
bootstrap; a promotion starts a new history whose parent is the old one.

parent_history_id.description: The history this one was promoted from; `null` for an original primary.

fork_offset.description: Changelog offset at which the promotion forked from the parent.

promoted_from.description: The primary the promoted standby had been following.

HostsImportInput.description: A hosts file to import into one zone.

text.description:
`/etc/hosts` format: `address name [name...]`, `#` comments. Names
without a dot are taken as relative to the zone.

mode.description:
`merge` (default) adds missing records; `replace` replaces every
record of the zone with the file's.

preview.description: Only parse and list what would be imported; change nothing.

HostsImportResult.description: What a hosts file holds for the zone, and what importing it changed.

skipped.description: Names not imported (outside the zone, loopback, unparseable).

HostsRecord.description: One record from a hosts file.

name.description: Relative to the zone (`@` for the apex).

HostsSkip.description: A name of a hosts file that is not imported, and why.

Identity.description:
Public identity (no authentication): lets a returning old primary find
out whether its peer was promoted away from its history.

ImportMode.description:
`merge` adds missing zones and records; `replace` replaces the records of
each zone in the document.

InterfaceStatus.description: One interface's addresses and which of them are bound.

bound.description: Addresses with a DNS listener (UDP and/or TCP) right now.

ListStatus.description: Download state of one list on this server.

entries.description: Domains in the copy in use (0 before the first good download).

skipped_lines.description: Lines not understood in the last good download.

capped.description: The list had more than the per-list maximum; the rest was ignored.

loaded_at.description: Time of the last good download.

error.description: Error of the last attempt (the last good copy stays in use).

blocked.description: Forwarded queries this list blocked since start.

interfaces.description:
`[server].interfaces` (per server): their current addresses and
which are bound; empty when `bind` is used.

status.description:
`ok`: signed in. `mfa_required`: POST /auth/mfa next.
`enroll_required`: scan `enroll` and POST /auth/enroll.

oneOf.description: TOTP enrollment data; non-null only when `status` is `enroll_required`.

LoginStatus.description: Next step after the password was accepted.

Member.description: A user granted access to a zone that is not its owner.

MemberRole.description: Role of a zone member (the owner is not a member).

used_recovery_code.description: True when a one-time recovery code (not a TOTP code) was used.

NotifyTargetView.description: One NOTIFY target from the config file.

key.description: Key that signs NOTIFY to this target; `null`: unsigned.

key_exists.description: False when `key` names a key that does not exist (then no NOTIFY is sent).

OverrideMode.description: How an override zone treats names it does not define itself.

ParentDsCheck.description: What the parent zone publishes, looked up through the forwarding upstream.

upstream.description: The resolver asked (the first forwarding upstream).

parent_ds.description: DS records the parent publishes (presentation form).

expected.description: DS records of this zone's key.

example.detail: no DS record for example.com. at the parent

force.description:
Promote even though the primary is currently reachable (two
writable servers until the old primary is stopped or fenced).

config_updated.description: Whether `[follow]` was removed from the config file.

notes.description: What to do next (config file, old primary).

QueryEvent.description: Emitted for every DNS query the server answers (streamed over `/ws`).

result.description:
What was returned, one entry per answer record in presentation form
("A 192.0.2.10", "CNAME www.example.com."), plus notes for referrals
and truncation. Capped in length; empty for negative answers.

source.description: auth | forward | cache | transfer | refused | error

filter.description:
The filter of the query pipeline that produced the answer (`edns`,
`request`, `special`, `transfer`, `authoritative`, `recursion`,
`open_resolver`, `forward`, ...); empty when the answer came before
the pipeline (a rejected TSIG signature).

ReauthBody.description: Body of `POST /me/mfa/start` when replacing an enrolled authenticator.

code.description: A current TOTP code of the enrolled authenticator.

RebindEntry.description: One name refused by rebinding protection.

address.description: The address that made the answer refused (last seen).

Record.description:
A record as stored. `name` is relative to the zone: `@` for the apex,
`www`, `*`, `_sip._tcp` and so on.

value.description: Presentation format, e.g. `10 mail.example.com.` for MX.

ttl.description: The record's TTL; `null` means the zone default TTL applies.

expires_at.description:
When the record stops being served (RFC 3339, UTC); `null` = never.
Expired records stay visible in the console and are deleted after
`[expiry].retention_days` (default 30).

RecordInput.description:
Input for creating or updating a record. Create: `type` is required,
`name` defaults to `@`. Update: omitted fields keep their current values,
including `ttl`; `"ttl": null` switches to the zone default.

ttl.description:
Omitted: keep the current TTL (update) or use the zone default (create).
`null`: zone default. A number: that TTL.

expires_at.description:
When the record stops being served, RFC 3339 (e.g. "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z").
Absent: keep the current expiry (update) or never expire (create).
`null`: never expire. Must be in the future. Do not combine with
`expires_in`.

RecordType.description: Record types the server stores and serves.

recovery_codes.description: Shown once; the previous codes stop working.

notes.description: What changed / what needs a restart.

ReplicaInfo.description: A replica as the API shows it.

conflict.description: The same id is used by two processes (addresses or sessions) at once.

applied_offset.description: The offset the standby has applied (the `after` of its last request).

lag_seconds.description: Seconds since the standby was last caught up (0 when it is).

user.description: The token user the standby authenticates as.

ReplicaReport.description:
`POST /replication/replicas/{id}/report`: a standby tells its primary
that it stopped (currently only `halted`).

example.detail: table users: differs (3 rows here, 3 on the primary)

read_only_reason.description: Why writes are refused (standby / fenced), else null.

replicas.description: Primary side: the standbys that follow this server, by instance id.

warning.description: A warning to show prominently (e.g. `[follow]` left in the config after promotion).

ReplicationSummary.description: Short replication summary in `GET /status` (every signed-in user).

primary.description: The primary (standby) or the peer that superseded this node (fenced).

problem.description:
Why a standby is not following (state `refused`: e.g. it has local
data and must be prepared with `--prepare-standby`), else null.

halted.description: Replication halted because the data diverged (see the status).

ResolverSettings.description:
Resolver behaviour for forwarded queries, set from the console
(Server settings -> Forwarding). Stored as the `resolver` setting
(replicated as `setting_set`); absent: the defaults. Fields missing from
a stored value (saved by an older version) take their defaults, and
fields this version does not know are ignored.

domain_needed.description:
`domain-needed`: never forward single-label names (`wpad`,
`printer`); they get NXDOMAIN here unless an own or override zone
has them. Default on.

bogus_priv.description:
`bogus-priv`: never forward reverse lookups of private and special
ranges (RFC 6303: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, 127/8,
169.254/16, 0/8, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ::1, ::); NXDOMAIN here unless
an own zone or automatic PTR covers the address. Default on.

rebind_protection.description:
`stop-dns-rebind`: forwarded answers that contain private,
loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA, `0.0.0.0` or `::` addresses are
refused. Never applied to own or override zones. Default off.

rebind_allow.description:
Domains (and everything below them) exempt from rebinding
protection (`rebind-domain-ok`).

serve_stale.description:
Serve stale (RFC 8767): when every upstream fails or times out,
answer from an expired cache entry (TTL 30 s). Default off.

max_stale_age_secs.description:
How long past its expiry a cache entry may still be served stale,
seconds (60 to 604800).

filter_types.description:
Record types never forwarded (`filter-AAAA`, `filter-rr`): such a
query gets an empty answer (NODATA) here. Default none.

ecs.description:
EDNS Client Subnet (`add-subnet`, RFC 7871) on forwarded queries.
Default off.

ecs_ipv4_prefix.description: Prefix of an IPv4 client address sent upstream (1 to 32).

ecs_ipv6_prefix.description: Prefix of an IPv6 client address sent upstream (1 to 128).

ecs_private_clients.description: Also send the subnet of clients in private and special ranges.

ResolverView.description: Resolver settings in effect, with what this server observed.

upstream_health.description: Health of the forwarding upstreams on this server, in order.

zone_upstreams.description: Health of the upstreams of each override zone with its own.

rebind_blocked.description:
Names refused by rebinding protection on this server, most recent
first (at most 100).

rebind_blocked_total.description: Answers refused by rebinding protection since start.

domain_needed_answered.description: Queries answered NXDOMAIN by `domain_needed` since start.

bogus_priv_answered.description: Queries answered NXDOMAIN by `bogus_priv` since start.

filtered_answered.description: Queries answered NODATA by `filter_types` since start.

Rights.description: Effective rights of a user (or of their API tokens).

zone_permissions.description: Legend: every zone permission and the minimum role it needs.

RoleSource.description: Where a zone role comes from.

ServerStatus.description: Server status, counters and runtime settings.

pipeline.description: The query pipeline in effect: its filters in order, with counters.

nsid.description: EDNS NSID reply; empty when off.

catalog_built_at.description: When the in-memory zone catalog was last rebuilt.

replication.description: Standby / primary role (the console shows a banner on a standby).

current.description: True for the session making this request (always false in the admin view).

oneOf.description: TOTP enrollment data; non-null only when `status` is `enroll_required`.

SettingSource.description: Where the forwarding settings in effect come from.

serial.description: Zone serial they were computed for.

next_resign.description:
When the primary re-signs (bumps the serial); null on a standby,
which follows the primary's re-signs.

Snapshot.description:
A consistent copy of everything replicated, read in one transaction,
as logical entities: the same facts as changelog changes (`user_created`,
`token_created`, `recovery_codes_replaced`, `tsig_key_set`,
`setting_set`, `zone_created`, `record_created`, `record_expired`,
`member_set`, ...). A standby loads it through the same replay code as
the changelog, so the format does not depend on the storage engine.

offset.description: The changelog offset this snapshot corresponds to: tail from here.

entities.description:
Users first, then their credentials and tokens, settings, TSIG keys,
zones, records and memberships (references come after their targets).

StatusResponse.description: Acknowledgement of an action without further data.

TableChecksum.description:
Checksum of one replicated table (local columns and the standby's own
root account left out).

tags.description:
Optional labels: at most 16, each 1-256 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`
after trimming (case is kept); duplicates are dropped.

token.description:
Plaintext `rdns_...` token; shown only once. Send as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

TokenInfo.description: An API token (never includes the secret).

tags.description:
Labels for finding and grouping tokens (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, case kept,
1-256 characters each, at most 16, sorted and de-duplicated).

last_used_at.description:
Last successful authentication with this token. Refreshed at most once
a minute (immediately when the client IP changes), so it may lag
real use by up to 60 seconds. `null`: never used.

last_used_ip.description:
Client IP of the last successful authentication (after trusted-proxy
resolution). `null`: never used.

tags.description:
The complete new tag list (replaces the old one; `[]` clears it).
At most 16, each 1-256 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` after trimming
(case is kept); duplicates are dropped.

TransferSettingsView.description:
The zone transfer policy in effect (`[transfer]` in the config file;
change it there and reload).

allow.description: Client networks allowed to request transfers. Empty: transfers disabled.

require_tsig.description: Transfers also need a valid TSIG signature.

port.description: DNS port this server listens on (for secondary configuration snippets).

warnings.description: Problems with the settings in effect, e.g. a NOTIFY key that does not exist.

require_tsig.description: Transfers also need a valid TSIG signature (`[transfer].require_tsig`).

TsigAlgorithm.description:
HMAC algorithm of a TSIG key. `hmac-sha1` is legacy: only for secondaries
that support nothing better.

TsigKeyCreated.description:
The created key and its secret. The secret is shown only here; later use
`POST /tsig/keys/{name}/reveal` (audited).

secret.description: Base64 secret, for the secondary's configuration.

name.description:
Key name: a DNS name, lowercase with a trailing dot. Secondaries must
use exactly this name.

zones.description: Zones this key may transfer. Empty: every zone.

TsigKeyInput.description:
A new TSIG key. Without `secret` a random one is generated (as long as
the hash: 32 bytes for hmac-sha256); with `secret` the base64 value your
secondary provider gave you is imported.

name.description: A DNS name such as `hn-secondary.` (a trailing dot is added; stored lowercase).

secret.description: Base64 secret to import (16 to 512 bytes). Omit to generate one.

zones.description: Zones this key may transfer. Omitted or empty: every zone.

TsigKeyZones.description: New zone scope of a key.

zones.description: Zones this key may transfer. Empty: every zone.

UpstreamHealth.description: Health of one upstream as this server saw it (I6).

latency_ms.description:
Average answer time (exponentially weighted, milliseconds); `null`
before the first answer.

consecutive_failures.description: Failures in a row (3 mark the upstream down).

down.description:
Marked down: skipped by the `fastest` and `parallel` strategies
except for one probe every 30 seconds.

UpstreamStrategy.description: How forwarded queries pick among the upstreams (I6).

ok.description: True when the upstream answered a recursive query for `. NS`.

ms.description: Round-trip time in milliseconds when it answered.

rcode.description: Response code when it answered, e.g. "No Error".

User.description: A user account as the API shows it (no secrets).

mfa_required.description: The user must enroll a TOTP authenticator at the next sign-in.

UserBody.description:
Create: `username` and `password` (min. 8 characters) are required.
Update: every field is optional; setting `password` or `disabled: true`
signs the user out everywhere. The root account's password is managed in
the config file.

mfa_required.description: The user must enroll a TOTP authenticator at the next sign-in.

UserWithRecoveryCodes.description: A user plus freshly generated recovery codes.

ip.description: Client IP as resolved by the server (proxy aware).

Zone.description: A zone as stored. Names are stored lower-case without the trailing dot.

name.description: Lower-case, no trailing dot (`.` for the root zone).

serial.description: SOA serial (unsigned 32-bit, so it may exceed the int32 range).

dnssec.description: DNSSEC signing is on (see `/zones/{zone}/dnssec`); absent when off.

signed_at.description:
DNSSEC signing epoch: the signature window starts one hour before
it and does not move when the zone changes; the primary sets it when
signing is turned on and when it re-signs. Absent: signing is off,
or the zone was signed by a version without it (the window then
follows `updated_at` until the zone's next change).

override.description:
Present for an override zone (I1): not authoritative, answered only
for clients allowed to use forwarding, names it does not define go
to its upstreams (`transparent`) or get NXDOMAIN (`static`). Absent
for an ordinary authoritative zone.

checksum.description: SHA-256 over the zone row, its records (with expiry state) and members.

records.description: First page of records (use /zones/{zone}/records to page or search).

members.description: Empty unless the caller may manage access (owner).

ZoneDetail.description: A zone with the first page of records and its members.

ZoneInput.description:
Input for creating or updating a zone. Create: `name` is required, other
fields fall back to server defaults. Update: omitted fields are left
unchanged (`name` is ignored).

owner.description:
Owner username. Create: defaults to the caller. Update: administrators
only; empty string clears the owner.

override.description:
Create: makes an override zone (I1) instead of an authoritative
one. Update: changes the mode or upstreams of an override zone (the
type itself is chosen at creation and cannot change).

ZoneOverride.description: The override settings of a zone (I1).

upstreams.description:
Upstreams for names this zone does not define (`ip:port`); empty:
the server's forwarding upstreams. An override zone without records
is conditional forwarding (`server=/example.com/10.8.0.1`).

mode.description: Default `transparent` on creation; unchanged when omitted on update.

ZonePerm.description:
Something a caller may do inside one zone. Granted when the caller's role
on the zone is at least [`ZonePerm::min_role`].

ZoneRights.description: The user's role on one zone and what it allows.

ZoneRole.description: What a caller may do with a zone.

ZoneUpstreams.description: Health of the upstreams of one override zone.

role.description: The caller's role on this zone.

ZoneView.description: A zone with the caller's view of it.

BadRequest.description: Invalid input: rejected by validation, or the request could not be parsed (`code: invalid_request`).

ConflictOrReadOnly.description: Conflicts with existing data, or this server is a read-only standby (`code: read_only_standby`; the message names the primary to use).

Forbidden.description: Not allowed, or cookie write without `X-Requested-With: rust-dns` (`code`: csrf).

InvalidRequest.description: Invalid request: malformed JSON, wrong field type or value, or an unparsable path or query parameter (`code: invalid_request`).

NotFound.description: Not found (zones the caller cannot see also return 404).

ReadOnly.description: This server is a read-only standby (or an old primary fenced after a failover): `code: read_only_standby`; the message names the primary to use.

example.error: this server is a read-only standby of https://dns1.example.net:8053; make changes on the primary

ServiceUnavailable.description: Too many password checks are running at once (they are CPU-bound and deliberately limited so DNS stays fast). Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

example.error: too many sign-ins or password changes in progress; retry in a moment

TooManyRequests.description: Too many attempts: the per-client rate limit (an IPv4 address or IPv6 /64), the account's failed-attempt back-off, or the session's code-attempt limit. `Retry-After` says when to try again.

example.error: too many failed attempts for this account; try again in 4 seconds

Unauthorized.description: Not signed in / invalid token (`code`: login_required, mfa_required, enroll_required).

cookie.name: rdns_session
cookie.description: Session cookie set by POST /auth/login (named `__Host-rdns_session` over HTTPS). Cookie writes also need `X-Requested-With: rust-dns`.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Sign in and out. Sign in here first (cookie session), or authorize with an API token.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The caller's own profile, password, MFA and sessions.

tags.name: Zones
tags.description: Create, inspect, update and delete zones.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: Search and edit resource records inside a zone.

tags.name: DNSSEC
tags.description: Per-zone DNSSEC signing (ECDSA P-256, NSEC): status, turning it on and off, the DS records for the registrar, a check of this server's signed answers and a lookup of the DS at the parent.

tags.name: Change log
tags.description: DNS change log, account audit log and the realtime WebSocket.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: API tokens for scripts and automation.

tags.name: Server
tags.description: Health, status, metrics and server administration.

tags.name: TSIG
tags.description: TSIG keys (RFC 8945) that authenticate zone transfers and NOTIFY for secondaries, and the transfer policy in effect (administrators).

tags.name: Replication
tags.description: Standby (follow) mode: what a standby pulls from its primary, replication status, and promotion of a standby. A standby refuses every mutating operation with 409 `read_only_standby`.
